subject: FY23 School Operating Budget Presentation
overview: The School Committee met for a special session to review the framework for the Fiscal Year 2023 operating budget, focusing on strategic priorities for student support and COVID-19 recovery. The administration presented a prioritized list of personnel and technology needs, totaling a developing budget request of approximately $71.4 million.

items.title: Call to Order and Meeting Logistics
items.summary: The meeting was called to order with a roll call and a brief overview of how the public could submit questions remotely.

items.title: FY23 Budget Development Process and Revenue Overview
items.summary: The administration outlined the budget cycle, noting that while the district faces uncertainty due to ongoing collective bargaining, it must balance one-time ESSER grant funds against recurring municipal revenue.

items.title: Fixed Cost Increases and Contractual Obligations
items.summary: Fixed costs were projected to increase by $2.5 million, driven by special education tuitions, transportation, and contractual salary steps.

items.title: Categorization of Strategic Priorities
items.summary: The administration introduced a categorization system (A-F) to distinguish between essential operating budget items and those suitable for one-time federal grant funding.

items.title: English Learner (EL) Staffing Requirements
items.summary: The Director of English Learners requested four additional teachers to manage a significant surge in newcomer student enrollment, which reached a record high of 577 students.

items.title: Mental Health and Counseling Positions
items.summary: The committee reviewed a request for three additional school adjustment councilors and the restoration of a career counselor position to address the increased social-emotional needs of students.

items.title: Health Services and Nursing Staffing
items.summary: The Director of Health Services proposed increasing the Curtis Tufts High School nurse to full-time status and retaining a float nurse for continued pandemic-related care coordination.

items.title: Special Education Personnel and Assistive Technology
items.summary: Proposed investments include one additional high school special education teacher to support rising enrollment and new funding for assistive technology and disability awareness training.

items.title: Instructional Technology and Maker Spaces
items.summary: The technology department prioritized installing interactive flat panels in 38 classrooms and expanding makerspace programming in elementary libraries.

items.title: Music, Arts, and Transportation Initiatives
items.summary: The administration recommended using ESSER funds to restock musical instruments, host a music summer camp, and continue providing free MBTA passes for students living over two miles from school.

items.title: School Lunch Program Funding Debate
items.summary: The committee debated the cost of universal free school lunch, with some members asserting it is established policy while the administration warned of significant financial uncertainty and a possible $1.5 million price tag.

items.title: Budget Request Summary and Adjournment
items.summary: The administration summarized the developing request at $71.4 million and confirmed that further deliberations on vocational and operational items would continue in subsequent meetings.
